text:
Anna L: Heads-up — proposing a small-but-impactful schema change for console telemetry/events. Goal: support route-level quotas and faster dashboard queries without huge joins. TL;DR: add a compact "route_key" (hash of route_id+profile) and a narrow metadata jsonb for sampling info, plus new composite PK on (tenant_id, route_key, event_ts).
Josh D: Quick Q — does this change the write path for every event? cost concerns for high-throughput tenants.
Anna L: Writes will be unchanged for now. Plan is dual-write to a shadow table (events_compact) for 2 weeks, then backfill. Primary table remains untouched during rollout. Only after validation we switch reads for console endpoints.
Priya S: From product: will existing dashboards keep working? We need minimal churn for customer-facing console queries.
Anna L: Yes — dashboard API will be behind a feature flag. Default stays on old tables. We add an opt-in flag per org to read from events_compact (faster aggregations). Then gradually flip orgs once metrics look stable.
Ben R: What about index size and retention? Adding composite PK could blow up storage and slow writes.
Josh D: Proposed indexes: primary on (tenant_id, route_key, event_ts DESC) and partial index for recent window (event_ts > now()-90d) to keep hot queries fast. Also use route_key as a small bytea (8 bytes) to avoid wide indexes.
Anna L: Example backfill SQL I'm proposing for shadow verification:

```
INSERT INTO events_compact (tenant_id, route_key, event_ts, kind, meta)
SELECT tenant_id,
       substring(md5(concat(route_id,':',profile)) from 1 for 16)::bytea as route_key,
       event_ts, kind,
       jsonb_build_object('sample_rate', coalesce(sample_rate,1)) as meta
FROM events
WHERE event_ts >= now() - interval '14 days'
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
```

Josh D: That looks fine. Can we make route_key computation deterministic in the application layer too? Avoid double computation during dual-write.
Anna L: Yes, we'll expose a small helper in our internal sdk (go/python) to compute route_key. We'll also add it to the ingestion API contract as an optional field for v2.
Priya S: UX ask — when we flip an org to compact reads, dashboards should surface whether data is coming from legacy or compact store. Instrumentation + console banner.
Ben R: Also add an SLO guard: if query latency from compact store exceeds legacy by >20% for a rolled org, auto-roll back to legacy for that org and create an alert.
Anna L: Agreed. Rollout plan summary:
- week 0: schema + migration scripts + sdk helper. dualwrite feature flag off.
- week 1-2: enable dualwrite (shadow write) for small canary orgs.
- week 3: run backfill for 14d window and compare aggregates.
- week 4-5: progressively opt-in read flag per org, monitor query latency and accuracy. auto-rollback threshold in place.
- week 6: if stable, schedule full cutover + remove legacy read paths.
Josh D: One more thing — telemetry metrics to collect: per-org cardinality of route_key, 95/99 latency for console queries, tokenized index size growth, and mismatch rate between legacy vs compact aggregates.
Anna L: We'll add those as grafana panels and create a dashboard README for the rollout owners.
Priya S: I can own dashboard copy and org communication. Will make a short help doc explaining why some orgs might see the new read flag.
Ben R: migrations-bot — create migration ticket and add a canary label.
migrations-bot: migration created: 20260318_0900_add_route_key_and_compact_events_table (PR: https://git.company/migrations/12345) :white_check_mark:
Josh D: Cool. I'll draft the backfill plan and window. Anna, can you add the SDK helper PR so I can wire dual-write?
Anna L: On it. Will drop PR link in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
Ben R: If anyone hits perf regressions while dualwriting, ping eng-oncall channel and tag me.
Anna L: Thanks everyone — will open the RFC doc with schema diagrams and sample queries. Thread closed for now, will update with PR links.
